messages.content:
"Imagine you are a chemist working in a lab. You have two samples of the same gas. The first sample has a quantity of 5 moles and is at a temperature of 300 Kelvin. The second sample has a quantity of 3 moles and is at a temperature of 500 Kelvin. You decide to mix these two samples together. What would be the final temperature of the mixture? 

Later, you obtain another gas sample with a quantity of 4 moles. You know that the molar mass of this gas is 16 g/mol. Can you calculate the mass of this gas sample?"

function.name: calculate_final_temperature
function.description: Calculate the final temperature when different quantities of the same gas at different temperatures are mixed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

quantity1.description: The quantity of the first sample of gas. This is a float type value.

temperature1.description: The temperature of the first sample of gas. This is a float type value.

quantity2.description: The quantity of the second sample of gas. This is a float type value.

temperature2.description: The temperature of the second sample of gas. This is a float type value.

function.name: calculate_mass
function.description: Calculate the mass of a gas given its quantity and molar mass. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

quantity.description: The quantity of the gas. This is a float type value.

molar_mass.description: The molar mass of the gas. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to compute final temperature mixing two gases (same gas). Use weighted average based on heat capacity proportional to amount if constant specific heat per mole. For ideal gas, internal energy U= n*Cv*T; Cv constant. So final T_f = (n1*T1 + n2*T2)/(n1+n2) assuming no work done etc.

Compute: (5*300+3*500)/8 = (1500+1500)/8=3000/8=375 K.

Second part: mass = quantity * molar mass = 4 moles * 16 g/mole = 64 grams.
